title: Snapmaker Orca · multiACE build
summary: Native multiACE emission is verified in a real slice. This chain adds the initial auto-load block and moves the topology settings onto the Multimaterial page.

features.what: Initial auto-load block before the prime line
features.why: One ACE_SWAP_HEAD per ACE-fed head at its first slot, in multiACE's own format and position, so head 3 no longer assumes it already holds the right colour.

features.what: multiACE topology moved to Printer settings → Multimaterial
features.why: Grouped per toolhead. The unit field no longer appears on heads with no ACE, which is what made the wrong field the obvious one to click.

features.what: Clearer labels for the two settings
features.why: "multiACE slots on this head (1 = stock feeder)" spells out that 1 means no ACE.

features.what: Central tool + temperature remap (already in the 10:26 binary)
features.why: T<n> and M104/M109 T<n> emit the physical head while per-filament settings still use the logical index.

verify: Restart Orca — the vendor version bump re-imports the U1 profiles (otherwise the cached copy in ~/.config/Snapmaker_Orca/system/ keeps winning).
Printer settings → Multimaterial: the four multiACE toolhead groups appear; Extruder pages no longer show them.
Slice the 7-colour cube and grep the gcode: '; multiACE auto-load' appears once, before ';===== 画起始线'.
Tool numbers stay T0–T3, and ACE_SWAP_HEAD carries ACE=0 for head 3.
open: Assignment dialog: page and optimiser are built and verified, but the C++ webview host and its slot in the send flow are not written yet.
Swap cost is not surfaced anywhere in the UI — the test cube prices at 300 swaps ≈ 15–20 m of purge.
"Fed by" pickers and Sync from printer are mockup-only (docs/ace-mmu/12-topology-config-ux.md).
